items.Sentence: Fine screens will be provided upstream of the MBR tanks to remove particulate material to avoid damaging the membranes.

The MBR process will consist of biological treatment utilizing anoxic, aerobic, and deoxygenation tanks, followed by submerged membrane ultrafiltration. The MBR process will remove carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand, nitrogen through nitrification and denitrification, and microbial solids removal through membrane separation.
Chloramine will be injected after the RO feed tank to prevent biological fouling of the RO membranes.
Sulfuric acid and antiscalant will be injected after the RO feed tank to control mineral scaling of the RO membranes.
Cartridge filters will be provided upstream of the RO membranes to remove particulate matter.

RO removes large molecular weight dissolved organic and inorganic compounds and pathogens by forcing MBR effluent through a semipermeable membrane under a higher pressure than the osmotic pressure of the solution.
The primary functions of UV/AOP include pathogen inactivation and destruction and removal of trace organic compounds.
Calcite and sodium hydroxide will be used for adjustment of pH, alkalinity, and hardness.
Sodium hypochlorite and liquid ammonium sulfate will be added post-stabilization to provide a 2 milligrams per liter (mg/L) chloramine residual in the product water tank and the distribution piping.

Odor from three foul air streams (fine screens, biological nutrient removal basins, and MBR tanks) will be captured, combined, and conveyed to a single odor control unit consisting of a single-bed carbon adsorber.
